memory_update.text: ECVT should be retained as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the sulphuric-acid node because its remaining core business is directly tied to virgin sulphuric acid, regeneration services and sulphuric-acid derivatives.
LXU should be retained as a small-cap industrial-acid/mining-input candidate, but later layers must verify sulphuric-acid revenue share and external merchant exposure before upgrading it.

KEX belongs in a speculative second-order logistics lane, not the direct acid-supplier lane, until specific sulphuric-acid, spent-acid, molten-sulphur or corrosive-chemical transport exposure is verified.

MOS is useful as a reference demand anchor: sulphur scarcity can pressure phosphate fertilizer economics through molten-sulphur-to-sulphuric-acid conversion, but MOS is not a pure bottleneck supplier.

Need a dedicated non-US or ADR/OTC pass for smelter-acid exporters in Japan, Korea, Canada and Europe; the US-listed universe may miss the most direct Asian smelter-acid beneficiaries referenced by Kpler.

Need a follow-up equipment pass for acid-resistant tanks, pumps, linings, heat exchangers, acid plants and EPC vendors; this pass found clearer US-listed chemical/logistics names than acid-equipment pure plays.

node: Sulphur and sulphuric-acid feedstock for copper SX-EW, nickel HPAL and fertilizers
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint. The most directly relevant underfollowed public names found in this pass are Ecovyst for virgin/regenerated sulphuric acid and LSB Industries for industrial sulphuric acid plus mining/industrial chemical adjacency. Kirby is a second-order logistics hypothesis because it controls a large US liquid-bulk tank-barge network for chemicals and agricultural chemicals, but specific sulphuric-acid cargo exposure still needs verification. Mosaic is included as a reference/context anchor rather than an alpha-discovery name: it is a large fertilizer producer that makes sulphuric acid internally from molten sulphur and is therefore exposed to sulphur feedstock availability and cost rather than being a pure bottleneck owner. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation.
